finance01.correction_to_initial_report: the initial report inferred an interface-based tailscale allow rule; NO such rule exists. The observed asymmetry is caused by bypasses, not by an allow rule.

bypasses.detail: tailscale inserts its own ACCEPT ahead of ufw (ts-input chain); tailnet traffic never reaches the 5 rules above
bypasses.proof: probed from the Mac at tailnet IP 100.95.238.12, which is NOT in 192.168.1.0/24
bypasses.conclusion: every 0.0.0.0 listener on finance01 is fully open to the whole tailnet; ufw stops none of it
bypasses.tailnet_membership: 5 nodes across two accounts - wx200.xyz@ (finance01, finance02, one Mac) and jiningluan@ (two Macs)
bypasses.how_to_restrict: tailscale ACLs in the admin console; adding ufw rules will not help

bypasses.detail: k8s NodePort traffic is DNATed in nat PREROUTING and lands in FORWARD, not INPUT, so ufw INPUT rules never see it
bypasses.evidence: 192.168.1.48:30810 open from finance02 while no ufw rule permits 30810; DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=ACCEPT
bypasses.origin: the ACCEPT was set to fix flannel VXLAN being dropped; backup at /etc/default/ufw.bak-quantlab
bypasses.confidence: inferred - not verified by reading iptables chains (needs sudo iptables -t nat -L PREROUTING -n)

mitigating_factors: NFS access is also gated by the export ACL (client IP), so a 100.x tailnet peer can reach 2049 but its mount is refused
k3s kubelet disables anonymous auth and requires client certs by default
